correctness.rationale: For every pair of edges the true intrinsic shortest path is classified explicitly. Counts of ordered same-edge, incident-edge, and disjoint-edge pairs exhaust all ordered edge pairs. The three elementary triangular CDFs give the formula on the entire support. Their CDF difference at fixed vertex count factors into a strictly positive threshold-dependent polynomial and a positive reciprocal-edge-count difference. The unique polynomial maximum gives exact total variation; its integral gives exact one-Wasserstein distance; limiting edge-pair weights give the asymptotics. The single-edge and star boundaries are consistent. A portable exact-rational checker independently computes vertex shortest routes and tests 40,570 cases, but the universal result is analytical.

value.rationale: The complete distribution and sharp first-order stochastic ordering across every bipartition of a fixed vertex set are natural transport-geometric invariants, strictly stronger than a mean comparison. The result quantitatively identifies a counterintuitive effect of edge densification under arclength sampling, with sharp decision thresholds, exact total-variation and one-Wasserstein separations, and an asymptotic gap of \(2/3\). These are universal family classifications, not isolated table entries or arbitrary numerical refinements. Fixed-vertex versus fixed-total-length scope is explicit.
